title: Bottoms on Bottoms!
summary:
Transporting Fuel Oil from Europe to the Far East
This week's report is based on a speech by Larry Axelrod of Poten & Partners on Transporting Fuel Oil from Europe to the Far East . The speech was made at the IPE/Confidence Conference on Fuel Oil and Heating Oil - Processing, Trading, Transportation in Antwerp, Belgium, on April 21-23. Russian Fuel Oil Exports Skyrocketing Russian seaborne exports of fuel oil from Baltic and Black Sea ports have nearly tripled from 15.8 million tons in 1998 to 43.2 million tons in 2004.

children.summary: While all tanker classes have benefited from the rising movement of fuel oil from Russia to China, the proportion of cargoes carried in larger-sized classes has been growing. For instance, VLCCs carried 39% of the volume of fuel oil in 2002 and 54% in 2004.

children.title: And of the Future?
children.summary: As long as China's economy keeps growing, even at a more subdued rate, fuel oil can be expected to continue to move in large quantities from Europe to the Far East over the coming years. For the complete text of Larry's speech, please contact Ms.
